mentioned.meaning: An opened page names the region (not the site) as an analog; today every such page is a Mars statement (docs/NOVELTY.md section 3).

power_info.source: NASA POWER climatology API v2 (MERRA-2), parameter TS annual (ANN) mean
power_info.period: January 2001 - December 2025 (as reported by the API header)
power_info.note: Earth annual mean skin temperature of the analog sites, to be set against lunar south-pole surface temperatures from job J13. Grid cells are about 50 km, so values describe the surroundings, not the exact site.

partner_info.sampling: the one pixel that holds the site centre; no averaging over the site

amsr2_smc_day.title: Soil Moisture Content (Daytime/Monthly-normal)
amsr2_smc_day.description: Volumetric water content over global land areas including arid and cold regions, except areas covered by vegetation with 2kg/m2 water equivalent. Accuracy is defined as mean absolute error of instantaneous observations.

amsr2_smc_night.title: Soil Moisture Content (Nighttime/Monthly-normal)
amsr2_smc_night.description: Volumetric water content over global land areas including arid and cold regions, except areas covered by vegetation with 2kg/m2 water equivalent. Accuracy is defined as mean absolute error of instantaneous observations.

caveats: Pixels of 2.6 km (SGLI), 5.6 km (MODIS) and about 11 km (AMSR2 grid; the footprint is larger) against sites of a few km: the values describe the surroundings of a site, not the site.

Satellite land surface temperature is a clear-sky skin temperature. The day mean, the night mean and their difference use only the months that have both values (*_diff_months): in polar regions these are spring and autumn only, so they are not annual means there.
SGLI is one year (2021); MODIS and AMSR2 are 2012-2021 monthly normals.
The day-night difference depends on the overpass times of each satellite; compare sites within one sensor, not across sensors.

ESA CCI Permafrost is a model product (MODIS surface temperature, ERA5, CryoGrid), north of about 16 N only; ground temperature is read for every grid chunk that holds a ranked or known site unless --ground-temp-chunks limits it (see permafrost.ground_temp_sites_not_read).
Nothing here enters the terrain score. The Moon has no air and no liquid water: these columns quantify where the analogy breaks and which sites are cold and dry, they do not close the gap.
Licence labels in both catalogues are 'proprietary' with links to the providers' terms; the terms have to be read and cited before publication (job J25).
